evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly into 'starting address is...' and logistics probing without first asking what Carson's biggest concerns or agenda items are.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by the customer during Section 2 (which never happened).
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised, so nothing to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers: property type (two bedroom apartment), floor/stories (second floor with elevator), number of rooms (two bedrooms plus living), special considerations (TV only, king bed, no heavy items, empty second bedroom), destination address and property type (two-story house, four bedrooms, driveway with cul-de-sac access), and box count estimate (25–35 typical, customer reports ~23 boxes from recent move, agrees 25–30 range). evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes: 'typically two bedroom apartment has 25 to 35 pre pack boxes. Do you think you're gonna be within the range or maybe if you were?'
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: No. Rep never asks 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full. Rep gives typical range ('two bedroom apartment takes two and a half to three and a half hours locally') and personalizes to this move ('since this is an out of town move I would estimate to move to take about six to eight hours'). Final estimate: '$2,448 to $2,864.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Rep discloses trip fee ($960), potential overnight fee ($240), notes no hidden fees, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, and 'time based so at the end of the day, you only pay for the actual time use on the move.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After pricing, rep asks 'Do you have any questions?' — not the Section 4 closing line. Customer responds 'Cool. No, that sounds good.' Rep does not ask 'Does that feel fair?' and does not hold silence.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. No version of 'Does that put those to rest?' asked. The call moves directly from pricing into the booking attempt.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. After customer raises his concern about the trip fee ('that's quite high as far as trip fee'), rep does not ask a genuine final-concerns check. The conversation ends without it.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No. Never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: With out. Rep says 'would you like to go ahead and lock in October 7th Wednesday?' — which is an explicit ask, but the customer deflects by saying he wants to shop other prices, and rep immediately pivots to 'Or you can also give us a call if ever you have any questions too' and 'just let us know.' This provides an easy out rather than holding the ask or re-engaging with the core concern.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None. The customer never commits. Rep does not confirm any booking details (date is assumed but not re-confirmed, no phone number taken, no arrival window, no crew size, no address confirmation, no crew notes about concerns). The call ends with 'just let us know.'

top_strength: Dana gathered all core logistics details efficiently and delivered a clear, anchored, and personalized estimate with full fee transparency in a conversational 5.6-minute call.
coaching_note: Never asked 'What are your biggest concerns about this move?' (Section 2), skipped both Promise deliveries entirely (Section 5), did not use 'Does that feel fair?' to close the estimate (Section 4), and abandoned the booking ask the moment the customer expressed price resistance instead of addressing his concern and re-engaging—this pattern turned a well-quoted move into a lost deal.
